rules.heading: Latch: refusals that set no latch (the list)
rules.quote: only add a wait for the owner to a miss that changed nothing. The list is read from the code (`main` in `hook-dispatch.mjs`), each item with the name that sets it, and a case holds its count to the list
rules.says: The list of no-latch refusals is read from the code (main in hook-dispatch.mjs), each item carries the name that sets it, and a test case holds the stated count to the list, so a refusal added to or dropped from the list changes the count and the case.
rules.enforcer: a case that holds the stated count to the list in hook-dispatch.mjs

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: a call held while a message from the owner waits, sent again once that message is delivered
rules.says: A call held while an owner message is waiting sets no latch; the session sends the same call again once that message is delivered.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: a stop from the owner standing, lifted by the owner's next message, a go-word
rules.says: A refusal because the owner's stop is standing sets no latch; the owner's next message, a go-word, lifts the stop.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: a correction from the owner standing, lifted by the owner's next message,
rules.says: A refusal because a correction from the owner is standing sets no latch; the owner's next message lifts it, and a latch would only wait on the owner a second time.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: a call held until the owner's messages filed at a compaction are read
rules.says: A call held until the owner's messages filed at a compaction have been read sets no latch; reading them answers it.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: a call held until the status page is read after a compaction
rules.says: A call held until the status page is read after a compaction sets no latch; reading the status page answers it.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: a main-thread call the manager fence refuses only because it is not of the record, a read of a path outside it or a tool or command line the fence does not pass
rules.says: A main-thread call the manager fence refuses only because it is not of the record (a read outside it, or a tool or command line the fence does not pass) sets no latch and is answered by a call the fence passes, which the refusal lists beside the check command.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: with it the dispatch gate's refusal of a step the plan's Steps did not hold when the plan was approved
rules.says: The dispatch gate's refusals of a step the approved plan's Steps did not hold, of a Standing step not on the Standing line then or neither the review nor a route check, and of any send once no Standing step names the review file by full path set no latch, and each is answered by a new plan through plan mode and the owner's button.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: with it the dispatch gate's refusal of a send while no approved plan is in force, answered by entering plan mode
rules.says: The dispatch gate's refusal of a send while no approved plan is in force sets no latch and is answered by entering plan mode.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: with it the dispatch gate's refusal of a send past the plan's priced count, answered by a new plan through plan mode that raises the line with the causes named
rules.says: The dispatch gate's refusal of a send past the plan's priced count sets no latch and is answered by a new plan through plan mode that raises the priced line with the causes named.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: a move the review gate refuses (the plan's first send and the first after an eject, a failure, a refusal or a correction)
rules.says: A move the review gate refuses (the plan's first send, and the first after an eject, failure, refusal or correction) sets no latch and is answered by sending the review step, by amending the plan's Steps or Order, or by entering plan mode.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: a send the rules gate refuses, because the plan pins a rules version the file has moved past
rules.says: A send the rules gate refuses because the plan pins a rules version the file has moved past sets no latch and is answered by a new plan through plan mode with the current version pinned and the owner's button.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: a send the reads gate refuses, answered by reading the refused file
rules.says: A send the reads gate refuses sets no latch and is answered by reading the refused file.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: the approval guard's refusal of a write of a finished plan's file, answered by entering plan mode and writing the next plan there
rules.says: The approval guard's refusal of a write to a finished plan's file sets no latch and is answered by entering plan mode and writing the next plan there.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: an agent's first refusal for the shape of a shell line (a `cd`, commands joined, a variable assignment in front, a write by redirect)
rules.says: An agent's first refusal for the shape of a shell line (a cd, joined commands, a leading variable assignment, a write by redirect) sets no latch and is answered by rewriting the line as the refusal says; the second such refusal latches the agent.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: the plan guard's refusal of a Bash line in plan mode that is not a read
rules.says: The plan guard's refusal of a Bash line in plan mode that is not a read sets no latch and no stop; it is answered by rewriting the line with readers or the Read and Grep tools.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: an Artifact publish the restored plan mode gate refuses, because the harness's plan mode began at a resume or a compaction after the approval
rules.says: An Artifact publish the restored plan mode gate refuses, because the harness's plan mode began at a resume or compaction after the approval and nothing has said so, sets no latch and is answered by saying so in a reply.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: an end of plan mode that the session's own exit call did not make, under any mode, which writes no approval marker and says so in the print
rules.says: An end of plan mode that the session's own exit call did not make writes no approval marker, says so in the print, and sets no latch, because the approval is the exit call's and not the app's.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: an agent's first call, refused by the plan fence because the agent has not yet read the rules
rules.says: An agent's first call refused by the plan fence because the agent has not yet read the rules sets no latch; the refusal text opens 'RULES FIRST, NO LATCH:'.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: the doctrine gate's refusal, answered by the Read of the doctrine it names
rules.says: The doctrine gate's refusal sets no latch and is answered by Reading the doctrine it names.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: the reply guard's refusal of the main thread's Read of a file of the record
rules.says: The reply guard's refusal of the main thread's Read of a file of the record sets no latch, because the reads gate already holds every send until a Read of that file has returned; a refusal of any other call keeps its latch and the text says which.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: the plan gate's refusal of the approval call for a name the session has not seen
rules.says: The plan gate's refusal of the approval call for a name the session has not seen sets no latch and is answered by a read that shows the name or by the file existing.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: the plan gate's refusal of the approval call for a plan already approved, when the harness's plan mode began at a compaction or a resume after the approval
rules.says: The plan gate's refusal of the approval call for an already approved plan, when the harness's plan mode began at a compaction or resume after the approval, sets no latch, unless the owner's newest typed message ends with a go-word and came after that plan mode began, in which case the call passes on the owner's go.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: the plan gate's refusal of the approval call for a fault of the plan's shape, a section missing, short or wrongly shaped
rules.says: The plan gate's refusal of the approval call for a fault in the plan's shape sets no latch and is answered by a write of the plan file, while the talk before the plan is the one refusal of that call that still latches.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: the app's identifier guard's refusal of the approval call, which still refuses and whose guard is untouched
rules.says: The app's identifier guard's refusal of the approval call sets no latch, though it still refuses and its guard is untouched.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: the dispatch gate's refusal of a send while the model serving the main thread is the top tier
rules.says: The dispatch gate's refusal of a send while the main thread is served by the top-tier model sets no latch and is answered by the owner's switch of model; the reply says so in its first line and ends as a declared stop.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: the plan gate's refusal of the approval call while the owner's newest typed message is recorded under auto mode
rules.says: The plan gate's refusal of the approval call while the owner's newest typed message is recorded under auto mode sets no latch and is answered by the session being out of auto mode and the call going up on a later message, so the approval is the owner's button.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: an end of plan mode made under auto mode with no exit call from the session, which records no approval and is said to be no approval
rules.says: An end of plan mode made under auto mode with no exit call from the session records no approval, is said to be no approval, sets no latch, and is answered by a new plan through plan mode with the session out of auto mode.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: the plan fence's refusal of an agent's call made at the moment the plan file is being re-recorded and no plan is in force, which says to send the same call again
rules.says: The plan fence's refusal of an agent's call made while the plan file is being re-recorded and no plan is in force sets no latch and says to send the same call again.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: The latch's own refusal repeats the original and writes no new latch
rules.says: A refusal made because a latch stands repeats the original refusal and writes no new latch.

rules.heading: Latch: refusals that set no latch (standing fact about plan-mode exit)
rules.quote: Measured 2026-10-03: the exit from plan mode in the app ended plan mode before the session's `ExitPlanMode` call was answered, the call came back "not in plan mode", no approval was recorded
rules.says: Standing fact: the app's exit from plan mode can end plan mode before the session's ExitPlanMode call is answered, so the call returns 'not in plan mode' and no approval is recorded, and a session must enter plan mode again rather than treat the plan as approved.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: The plan fence's refusals and the dispatcher's list above are decided apart:
rules.says: A step that adds a refusal to plan-fence.mjs must list hook-dispatch.mjs among its files and add the refusal's words to the no-latch list where the refusal must set no latch, because the fence refuses and the dispatcher decides by fixed refusal words whether it latches.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: `hook-dispatch.mjs` (`releaseCommand`, `releaseLifts`): the reply guard's release command, `node reply-guard.mjs --read` with its arguments as one plain command
rules.says: The reply guard's release command, node reply-guard.mjs --read with its arguments as one plain command, passes the manager fence as the status command does and passes the latch on the main thread, and a release of the call the latch was set by lifts that latch.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: A latch another guard set, an agent's own latch and a release of another call stand.
rules.says: A latch another guard set, an agent's own latch, and a release of a different call than the one that set the latch are not lifted by the release command and stand.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: The refusal of the reply guard that names the command says so (LESSONS §432).
rules.says: The reply guard's refusal that names the release command must say what the release does and does not lift.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: A Stop refusal never latches.
rules.says: A refusal at Stop never sets a latch.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: While the main thread's latch stands, every PreToolUse call on the main thread and in agents is refused except five kinds, read from `main` in `hook-dispatch.mjs`
rules.says: While the main thread's latch stands, every PreToolUse call on the main thread and in agents is refused except five kinds: the status command with the --can check and plan check (main thread only), TaskStop (main thread only), the reply guard's release command (main thread only), a latched agent's own progress note and report step-N.txt and step-N-report.txt in progress/ of the session scratchpad for the step its prompt names, and an agent's own return, which passes every guard.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: **A refusal INSIDE an agent latches that agent only.** It is written under that agent's id: every later call of that agent is refused but its own return
rules.says: A refusal inside an agent latches that agent only, written under its id, so every later call of that agent is refused except its own return, while the main thread and other agents are not held; a refusal on the main thread latches the main thread and with it every agent.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: Nothing clears an agent's latch, because its one move is its own return.
rules.says: Nothing clears an agent's latch, so a latched agent's one move is to return what it has with the refusal's text.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: The main thread reads the agent's refusal from the status print (rule 2), which carries every hook refusal each agent received, and reports it
rules.says: The main thread reads an agent's refusal from the status print, which carries every hook refusal each agent received, and reports it, so the owner hears of it in the status and never as a latch on the session.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: The main thread's `TaskStop` passes the main thread's latch because stopping a task changes none of the owner's work and the session owns what it started (§11d)
rules.says: The main thread's TaskStop passes the main thread's latch, because stopping a task changes none of the owner's work and the session owns what it started.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: An agent's `TaskStop` and the wait between statuses stay refused.
rules.says: An agent's TaskStop and the wait between statuses stay refused while a latch stands, and the refusal names the original refusal.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: An agent cannot stamp a status at all, latched or not: the dispatcher refuses the status command from an agent
rules.says: An agent never runs the status command, latched or not, because an agent cannot tell the owner anything and its stamp would mark the main thread's status as given when none was.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: `stop-guard.mjs` lets a latched session stop.
rules.says: A latched session is allowed to stop; the stop guard does not refuse a stop because of a latch.
rules.live_quote: `stop-guard.mjs` is a shell that never refuses a stop. (LESSONS §434, §459.)
rules.missing: The live line says the stop guard never refuses a stop. It does not say anything about a latched session, and no live page describes a latch.

rules.heading: 14. A refusal latches until the owner's next message.
rules.quote: Only a message the owner typed after the latch clears it, by the time it was typed rather than when it was delivered
rules.says: Only a message the owner typed after the latch was set clears it, judged by the time it was typed and not when it was delivered; a task notification, a scheduled message, an agent's return and a message typed before the refusal clear nothing.

rules.heading: Latch: what clears it (what counts as a message from the owner)
rules.quote: as `isOwnerMessage` in `transcript-tail.mjs` tells an owner's message
rules.says: Whether a message is the owner's is decided by isOwnerMessage in transcript-tail.mjs, and the harness queues a message the moment it is sent and delivers it later, which is why the time typed and not the time delivered is used.

rules.heading: 15. A statement of state is read, never remembered.
rules.quote: **A statement of state is read, never remembered.** What state a task, an agent, a branch, a push, a deploy, a file, a workflow, a run, a commit, a
rules.says: The state of a task, agent, branch, push, deploy, file, workflow, run, commit, build, release, CI, pipeline, worktree, the working copy or a remote is read in the same turn and said from the read.
rules.live_quote: - A statement of state is read in the same turn, never remembered.
rules.missing: The named list of states (task, agent, branch, push, deploy, file, workflow, run, commit, build, release, CI, pipeline, worktree, working copy, remote) and the 'I think' fallback with the offer of the check or asking the owner first.

rules.heading: 15. A statement of state is read, never remembered.
rules.quote: Otherwise the sentence says "I think" and the reply offers the check, or, when checking would be a big job, the question goes to the owner first.
rules.says: When a state has not been read in the same turn, the sentence says 'I think' and the reply offers the check, or, when checking would be a big job, asks the owner first; a reply stating such a state with no tool result in that turn is refused unless it says 'I think' and asks whether to run the check.

rules.heading: 15. A statement of state is read, never remembered (limits of the guard)
rules.quote: It cannot tell which read backs which sentence, so one read in the turn lets every claim in the reply through; and it reads words, so a claim worded in a way its patterns do not know passes it.
rules.says: The stop guard cannot tell which read backs which sentence, so one tool result in the turn lets every claim through, and it reads words, so a claim worded in a way its patterns do not know passes it; the session must therefore read the state behind every such claim itself and not rely on the guard to catch the rest.
